design_detail: US National Comorbidity Survey (1990–1992), household sample aged 15–54; lifetime use and DSM-III-R dependence by substance class; conditional probability of dependence among people who had ever used each class.
can_establish: Among people who had ever used each substance class, the share who had ever met dependence criteria, in that population and period.
cannot_establish: Current risk (data are three decades old; potency, products and context have changed); methamphetamine-specific risk (grouped under 'stimulants').

outcomes.operationalization: Lifetime dependence among people with lifetime use.

analysis.effect_sizes: Conditional probabilities by class ([to be extracted from PDF], Table [to be extracted from PDF]): tobacco about 32%, heroin about 23%, cocaine about 17%, alcohol about 15%, stimulants about 11%, cannabis about 9%.

interpretation_gap.results_show: Most people who had ever used each class had not met dependence criteria.
interpretation_gap.claimed: Widely quoted as '80–90% of users never become addicted'; the figure varies by substance and the study is old.

timeline.event: NESARC survival analysis gives lifetime cumulative transition probabilities for nicotine, alcohol, cannabis and cocaine

replication.where_it_stands: The ranking of substances is stable across surveys; absolute figures vary by era and definition.

funding.funder: NIMH and others [to be extracted from PDF]

what_would_settle_it: Contemporary cohorts with current products and ICD-11/DSM-5 criteria.

risk_of_bias.reasoning: Strong survey; the limitation is age and indirectness, not bias. Provisional: these JBI judgments were made from the abstract when the card was drafted (source_read: abstract only); the response rate and the definition of stimulant use are to be checked in the full text, and the claim citing this card records one provisional risk-of-bias level until then.

editorial_corrections.reason: Language (METHODS §9): 4 replacements, no change of meaning, number or citation; list in data/verification/language-2026-10-16.json

Written from the abstract on 2026-10-14 for the first prototype, with placeholders where the PDF is needed; a card written from an abstract alone cannot leave draft (METHODS §5.5; methods audit M33). It is rewritten from the full text when the PDF is saved.

disagreements.first_pass: Strong survey; the limitation is age and indirectness, not bias.
disagreements.resolution: Applied by the editor after adjudication against the source: Review round 2 (group P, finding 13): the claim now records risk of bias as one provisional level because the paper has not been read; the card's JBI 'low' was judged from the abstract, which the reasoning should say. Labelling, not a change of judgment; the judgment itself is for the readers once the PDF is read (METHODS §5.3).
